introduction: Lear intends to retire from government while retaining the honors and companionship of kingship. His decision to measure his daughters' love through public declarations turns the division of Britain into a test that rewards persuasive speech and punishes plain dealing. Gloucester's household faces a related crisis when his illegitimate son Edmund challenges the inheritance reserved for Edgar. As fathers misjudge their children and faithful servants face exclusion, private family choices begin to reshape the country's political order.

fullSynopsis.text: Lear divides his kingdom according to his daughters' declarations of love. Goneril and Regan flatter him, but Cordelia refuses to inflate her duty into an exclusive devotion. Enraged, Lear disinherits her and banishes Kent for protesting. France accepts Cordelia without a dowry, while Lear gives government to the elder daughters and their husbands, reserving a hundred knights and alternate residence with them. Gloucester meanwhile believes a forged letter through which Edmund frames Edgar as a threat to their father's life. Edmund warns the unsuspecting Edgar to hide, presenting himself as his protector.

Kent returns disguised to serve Lear. Goneril orders neglect of her father and demands a reduction of his retinue, describing the knights as disorderly. Lear curses her and leaves for Regan, while the Fool repeatedly exposes the folly of giving away his power. Edmund stages an encounter with Edgar, wounds himself, and persuades Gloucester that Edgar attacked him for resisting a murder plot. Edgar flees and disguises himself as the mad beggar Poor Tom. At Gloucester's castle Cornwall and Regan put Kent in the stocks. The daughters then unite in reducing Lear's permitted followers toward none. Refusing dependence on those terms, Lear goes into the storm, and they shut the doors.

On the heath Lear challenges the elements as his mind breaks under grief. Kent seeks shelter and sends news toward Cordelia and the arriving French force. Lear's suffering also awakens concern for people who endure homelessness without royal protection. In the hovel he encounters Edgar, whose feigned madness Lear interprets through his own daughters' betrayal. Gloucester secretly shelters the king despite orders against helping him. Edmund discloses his father's contact with France to Cornwall and gains his title. After Lear conducts an imaginary trial of his daughters, Gloucester arranges his escape to Dover. Cornwall tears out Gloucester's eyes as Regan urges the punishment. A servant wounds Cornwall trying to stop the cruelty, and Regan kills the servant. Learning that Edmund betrayed him, Gloucester recognizes Edgar's innocence.

Still concealing his identity, Edgar guides the blinded Gloucester toward Dover. Gloucester wants to die by jumping from a cliff, but Edgar stages a harmless fall on level ground and persuades him that the gods have preserved him. Cornwall's death leaves Regan free to compete with Goneril for Edmund, while Albany condemns the sisters' treatment of Lear. Cordelia seeks her father with an army whose purpose she describes as his restoration. Lear meets Gloucester in a mixture of madness and insight into power and injustice. When Oswald attacks Gloucester, Edgar kills him and discovers Goneril's letter urging Edmund to dispose of Albany. Rest and care allow Lear to recognize Cordelia and ask her forgiveness; she answers with love.

Albany joins the defense against France while separating that cause from the wrongs done to Lear. Edgar gives him Goneril's incriminating letter. Edmund has promised himself to both sisters and intends to prevent Albany's mercy toward Lear and Cordelia. The British forces win, and the reunited father and daughter become prisoners. Lear imagines a peaceful life with Cordelia even in confinement, but Edmund secretly commissions their deaths. Albany arrests Edmund for treason and challenges him to answer a champion. Edgar appears, defeats his brother, and reveals his identity. He reports that Gloucester died from mingled joy and grief when he finally recognized his son.

Goneril poisons Regan and kills herself when her plot is exposed. Wounded Edmund attempts to revoke his execution order, but Cordelia has already been hanged. Lear enters carrying her body after killing her executioner and vainly searches for signs of life. Edmund's death is reported. Albany proposes restoring Lear's power and the faithful men's rights, but Lear dies over Cordelia. Albany asks Kent and Edgar to sustain the ruined state. Kent anticipates following his master in death, and Edgar closes with the burden of surviving such suffering. No recovery of family or kingdom can undo the losses before them.

acts.label: ACT I
acts.summary: Lear rewards Goneril and Regan's professions of love with shares of Britain, then disinherits Cordelia for speaking plainly about her duty and banishes Kent for defending her. France takes Cordelia without a dowry. Lear transfers government while retaining his royal title, a hundred knights, and the expectation of living with each elder daughter in turn. Edmund fabricates a letter to make Gloucester believe Edgar seeks his death, then persuades Edgar that hiding is necessary for safety. Kent returns in disguise and enters Lear's service. Goneril encourages disrespect toward her father and demands fewer followers. Lear curses her and leaves for Regan. The Fool's jokes repeatedly expose the consequences of surrendering power, while Lear begins to regret his judgment and fears madness.

acts.label: ACT II
acts.summary: Edmund sends Edgar fleeing after a sham fight, wounds his own arm, and tells Gloucester that his brother attacked him for opposing their father's murder. Gloucester promises to make Edmund capable of inheriting his lands; Edmund also gains Cornwall's confidence. Hunted as a traitor, Edgar adopts the appearance and speech of Poor Tom, a wandering mad beggar. Kent attacks Goneril's messenger Oswald and is placed in the stocks by Cornwall and Regan, despite the insult to Lear's authority. Arriving at Gloucester's castle, Lear discovers the humiliation and still hopes for Regan's support. She instead sides with Goneril. Together the sisters reduce the number of followers they will receive, finally questioning his need for any. Lear leaves in anguish as the storm rises, and the household closes its doors.

acts.label: ACT III
acts.summary: Kent sends a gentleman toward Cordelia with news of Lear, then guides the king and Fool toward shelter. Lear rages against the storm and his daughters, but also begins to understand the exposure of the poor. Edgar, disguised as Poor Tom, becomes his supposed philosopher. Gloucester defies the daughters' orders by bringing food and shelter; Edmund reports his father's secret support for the king and connection with France to Cornwall. Lear stages a deranged trial of Goneril and Regan before Gloucester arranges his removal to Dover. Cornwall and Regan seize Gloucester, and Cornwall tears out his eyes at Regan's urging. A servant resisting the torture wounds Cornwall and is stabbed by Regan. Regan tells Gloucester that Edmund betrayed him, making the blinded father understand that Edgar was falsely accused.

acts.label: ACT IV
acts.summary: Edgar takes charge of Gloucester without revealing himself and promises to lead him to Dover's cliff. Albany reproaches Goneril, while news of Cornwall's death intensifies the sisters' rivalry over Edmund. Cordelia searches for Lear and seeks treatment for his distress; Kent explains that shame has made him reluctant to meet her. Edgar simulates a cliff-top on level ground, then tells Gloucester that surviving his attempted leap proves divine protection, giving him reason to endure. They encounter Lear, whose wandering speech exposes injustices as well as confusion. Edgar kills Oswald when he tries to murder Gloucester and finds Goneril's plot against Albany. Lear is finally brought to Cordelia's care, wakes from restorative sleep, recognizes her, and asks forgiveness, receiving a loving answer.

acts.label: ACT V
acts.summary: Edmund manages the sisters' jealous promises and plans to frustrate Albany's intended mercy. Edgar gives Albany the letter exposing Goneril's murderous design. Lear and Cordelia lose the battle and are imprisoned; Edmund sends secret orders for their deaths. Albany arrests him, and Edgar defeats him in single combat before revealing his identity. Edgar reports Gloucester's death following their reunion. Goneril's poisoning of Regan and her own suicide are announced, and their bodies appear. Edmund tries to rescind the killings, but Lear enters with Cordelia already dead. He has killed her executioner and now desperately hopes she may breathe. Edmund dies, and Lear follows while mourning Cordelia. Albany asks Kent and Edgar to rule; Kent anticipates death, and Edgar speaks the final words of grief.
